submitted.test_code:
import math
from checkout.pricing import compute_total


def test_single_percent_coupon_takes_exactly_ten_percent():
    items = [{"price": 100.00, "qty": 1}]
    coupon = {"kind": "percent", "value": 10}
    base = compute_total(items, [])
    discounted = compute_total(items, [coupon])
    assert math.isclose(base, 100.00, abs_tol=0.005)
    assert math.isclose(discounted, base - 10.00, abs_tol=0.005)
    assert math.isclose(discounted, 90.00, abs_tol=0.005)
submitted.what_it_checks: A single 10% percent coupon on a 100.00 subtotal gives exactly 90.00 (no-coupon total minus 10%), not 80.00.

report.root_cause: Payment timeouts began rising at 13:50 UTC, about 20 minutes before the v1.4.2 deploy, and match PayFast's reported us-east API latency and timeout degradation since 13:50. The most likely cause is the external payment provider (PayFast) degradation, not our deploy. Timeouts plateaued at 14:00–14:09 and showed no additional step at 14:10.
ruled_out: The v1.4.2 deploy is ruled out as the trigger because timeouts and error rate rose at 13:50, before the 14:10 deploy, with no further step afterward.
The log-format change is ruled out as an artifact because the rise appears in metrics, not just log counts, and predates 14:10.
A traffic surge is ruled out because orders per minute stayed flat at about 19.5–20.3/min.
A change in order mix is ruled out because average order value stayed flat at about $73–75.
report.suggested_fix: Treat this as a PayFast us-east incident: track the provider status, consider failover to another region or provider or extended retry/backoff if available, and reconcile unpaid orders once PayFast recovers.
